title: Local factorization of $f^!$ on an affine chart
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p_0>0$ with $p_0\ne\ell$, an algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it. Let $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with the following condensed coefficient convention. For $E$, the coefficient ring has sections $S\mapsto C(S,E)$ on profinite sets, with the $\ell$-adic topology, as in [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use the coefficient ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], whose sections on a profinite set $S$ are the continuous maps $S\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ with image contained in some finite subextension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, and $f:X\to Y$ a separated finite-type $k$-morphism, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Use the module-object pro-etale categories $\Dbc(-,\Lambda)$ of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], their localizing closures [sk-def-localizing-closure], and the exceptional right adjoints of [sk-prop-sf-existence]. Write $a^*=La^*$ for derived pullback [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

Let $v:V\hookrightarrow Y$ and $u:U\hookrightarrow X$ be affine open subschemes with $f(U)\subset V$, let $d\ge0$, let $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_V$ be a closed immersion over $V$, and let $p:\mathbf A^d_V\to V$ be the projection [def-sbc-affine-space], so $fu=vpi$. Then there is an isomorphism of functors
$$
u^*f^!\simeq i^!p^!v^*:\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))\longrightarrow\Loc(\Dbc(U,\Lambda)),
$$
and $u^*f^!K\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$ for every $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$. There exists a finite family of such data $(V,U,i,d)$ whose opens $U$ cover $X$.

proof.text: The field $k$ is Noetherian, since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], $X,Y$ are Noetherian and quasi-compact. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated] they are quasi-separated. Each affine open immersion into $X$ or $Y$ is quasi-compact: its inverse image of any affine open is the intersection of two affine opens, which is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion]. By [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type] these affine open immersions are of finite type. Composing their local finite-type property with the structure morphisms of $X,Y$, using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e), shows that $U,V$ are locally of finite type over $k$; they are quasi-compact because affine, hence of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

proof.text: The affine space over the affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is $\operatorname{Spec}A[t_1,\ldots,t_d]$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. This polynomial algebra is generated over $A$ by its coordinates, so its projection is of finite type; it is separated since its diagonal is cut out on the two-factor polynomial ring by $t_j-s_j$, a closed immersion by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The inclusions of the open subschemes $U,V$ are separated: their relative diagonals are isomorphisms, since they are open-subscheme inclusions. Composing with the separated structure morphisms of $X,Y$ using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) proves that $U,V$ are separated over $k$. For $\mathbf A^d_V$, compose the locally finite-type projection with $V\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e); since $\mathbf A^d_V$ is affine, it is quasi-compact, so its structure map is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. The polynomial-diagonal calculation and the separatedness of $V$ prove that $\mathbf A^d_V$ is separated over $k$ by the separated-composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e). Thus $U,V,\mathbf A^d_V$ remain in the standing separated finite-type setting, and are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], hence quasi-compact, and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

proof.text: By [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc], $\Dctf=\Dbc$ and their localizing closures agree on all these schemes for our two coefficient fields. The adjunctions of [sk-prop-sf-existence] therefore have exactly the localizing categories displayed in the item. The given closed immersion $i$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c), hence separated and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus the chart maps $u,v,i,p$ all satisfy the morphism hypotheses of the adjunction and composition statements. More generally, each separated finite-type $k$-scheme is qcqs by these two Noetherianity statements, so [det-def-localizing-closure-ctf-equals-bc] identifies $\Dctf$ and $\Dbc$ on every standing scheme used below.

proof.text: Choose finitely many affine opens $V_\beta$ covering $Y$, by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover] and steps 1–3. For each $V_\beta=\operatorname{Spec}A_\beta$, the finite-type condition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] provides a finite affine cover $U_{\beta\alpha}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{\beta\alpha}$ of $f^{-1}(V_\beta)$ with $B_{\beta\alpha}$ finitely generated over $A_\beta$. These are affine opens in $X$, their composite maps to $Y$ factor through $V_\beta$, and the finite family of all $U_{\beta\alpha}$ covers $X$. This uses the finite-algebra affine cover that the finite-type definition supplies, rather than an unproved assertion about an arbitrary chosen affine cover.

source.place: Existence of charts, first two sentences; Stacks Tags 01IT and 01T2.

proof.text: For one of the pairs $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ of step 4, choose algebra generators $b_1,\ldots,b_d$ of $B$ over $A$. Evaluation $A[t_1,\ldots,t_d]\to B$, $t_j\mapsto b_j$, is surjective: its image is an $A$-subalgebra containing all the chosen generators, hence all of $B$. By the affine closed-immersion description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], this surjection gives $i:\operatorname{Spec}B\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}(A[t_1,\ldots,t_d])=\mathbf A^d_{\operatorname{Spec}A}$, using [def-sbc-affine-space]. Its composite with $p$ corresponds to the original map $A\to B$, so $fu=vpi$. Repeating this construction for the finite family in step 4 proves the existence clause. The case $d=0$ is allowed.

source.place: Existence of charts, last sentence; Stacks Tag 01QO (morphisms.tex, lemma-closed-immersion, equivalence of (1) and (2)).

proof.text: For composable separated finite-type $k$-morphisms $S\xrightarrow{a}T\xrightarrow{b}W$ between standing schemes, [lem-sfb-localizing-lower-shriek-composition] gives the natural isomorphism $Rb_!Ra_!\simeq R(ba)_!$, with the same compactification-defined functors and the finite-subextension condensed coefficient convention at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Step 3 identifies the localizing $\Dctf$ categories in that statement with the localizing $\Dbc$ categories here.

source.place: The composition isomorphism paragraph; proper/open interchange and compactification comparison; Stacks Tag 0D6E, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition.

proof.text:
For any composable separated finite-type morphisms $S\xrightarrow{a}T\xrightarrow{b}W$ in the standing setting, step 6 gives $R(ba)_!\simeq Rb_!Ra_!$ on the localizing closures. The adjunctions [sk-prop-sf-existence] and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] give natural bijections, for $A\in\Loc(\Dbc(S,\Lambda))$ and $B\in\Loc(\Dbc(W,\Lambda))$,
$$\operatorname{Hom}(R(ba)_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Rb_!Ra_!A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(Ra_!A,b^!B)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(A,a^!b^!B).$$
Thus $a^!b^!$ and $(ba)^!$ are right adjoints of the same functor. By [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] they are naturally isomorphic, $(ba)^!\simeq a^!b^!$. Step 3 identifies the $\Loc(\Dctf)$ categories of the cited statements with the displayed $\Loc(\Dbc)$ categories. This is rational module-object compact supports on whole localizing closures; no finite-torsion-only composition theorem is substituted.

source.place: The factorization paragraph: composition of exceptional adjoints, with the natural Hom-bijection argument written out.

proof.text:
For the quasi-compact open immersions $u$ and $v$, clause (1) of [det-sf-mate-open-restriction] gives $u^!\simeq u^*$ and $v^!\simeq v^*$. Apply the composition formula of step 7 first to $u,f$, then to $pi,v$, and then to $i,p$. Since $fu=vpi$ as scheme morphisms, it gives the natural chain
$$u^*f^!\simeq u^!f^!\simeq(fu)^!=(vpi)^!\simeq (pi)^!v^!\simeq i^!p^!v^!\simeq i^!p^!v^*.$$
These are isomorphisms on the whole localizing closures, with source $\Loc(\Dbc(Y,\Lambda))$ and target $\Loc(\Dbc(U,\Lambda))$. The open immersions are quasi-compact and all source schemes are qcqs by steps 1–3; their coefficients are admissible because they are the two rational fields fixed in the statement.

source.place: The factorization paragraph, entire displayed chain, and the open-immersion adjunction assertion immediately preceding it.

proof.text: Let $K\in\Dbc(Y,\Lambda)$. By step 3 it belongs to $\Dctf(Y,\Lambda)$. Apply [det-proper-base-change-unbounded-pullback] to $v$: its statement gives $v^*K\in\Dctf(V,\Lambda)$, hence $v^*K\in\Dbc(V,\Lambda)$. By [det-cor-affine-space-rational-induction], $p^!\simeq p^*(d)[2d]$ and this functor maps $\Dbc(V,\Lambda)$ into $\Dbc(\mathbf A^d_V,\Lambda)$. Thus $H=p^!v^*K$ is bounded constructible, including $d=0$.

Let $O=\mathbf A^d_V\setminus U$ be the open complement of the chart's closed immersion. The ambient affine space is Noetherian by steps 1–3. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian], $O$ is Noetherian and quasi-compact; its open inclusion is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1), hence finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type]. Its diagonal is an isomorphism, so it is separated. Compose its locally finite-type and separated structure morphisms using [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e); since $O$ is quasi-compact, [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] makes $O$ a separated finite-type $k$-scheme. Thus the support theorem's ambient scheme, closed subscheme, and open complement all lie in the standing setting.

For the closed-immersion normalization, compute compact support using the compactification $(\operatorname{id}_U,i)$, which is allowed because $i$ is proper by steps 1–3. The definition [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek] and comparison [det-sf-comp-coherence-cocycle] identify the chosen $Ri_!$ with $Ri_*$. The exact closed direct image in [det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-support] has $Ri_*=i_*$ by the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Precomposing the adjunction Hom bijection with this natural comparison and applying [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identifies its right adjoint with the closed-normalized one. Apply [det-prop-closed-adjoint-constructible-yoneda] to $i:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^d_V$ and the bounded constructible $H$ of step 9. It gives $i^!H\simeq R\underline\Gamma_UH$. The support statement's $\Dbc$ is the weaker locally-finitely-presented one; for the finite-constant-local-model $\Dbc$ apply [lem-sfb-rational-closed-support-constructible] to $i$ and $H$: it gives $R\underline\Gamma_UH\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$. Consequently $i^!p^!v^*K\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$. The coefficient fields carry precisely the pulled-back condensed structures in the support and Yoneda statements.

Evaluate the functor isomorphism of step 8 at $K$. It identifies $u^*f^!K$ with the bounded constructible object of step 10, so its cohomology sheaves are isomorphic to the same constructible sheaves and vanish outside the same finite interval. Thus $u^*f^!K\in\Dbc(U,\Lambda)$, as claimed.
